title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s end-to-end applied ML evaluation workflow: onboarding models into the eval harness, designing and curating prompt sets and benchmarks, applying and validating quantization profiles, and triaging regressions. It consolidates operational checklists, acceptance criteria, and step-by-step procedures intended for ML engineers, applied ML, and SREs responsible for model serving quality.

Purpose and scope:
- Provide a single reference for onboarding new models into the eval harness and production serving pipelines.
- Standardize prompt set design and benchmark construction to ensure reproducible comparisons across model families and quantization profiles.
- Provide guardrails and automated checks to detect quality regressions early in the model lifecycle.
- Define a triage playbook for regressions with clear owners, timelines, and rollback/fallback actions.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers, model owners, serving runtime engineers, platform SREs, and product managers.

Key definitions:
- Eval harness: The standardized test harness used to run batched evaluations across models, prompts, and metrics (precision: exact-match, semantic similarity, toxicity checks, latency/cost).
- Prompt set: Curated collection of inputs designed to exercise specific model capabilities or failure modes.
- Quantization profile: A set of bit-depth, per-layer, and kernel settings used to reduce model memory/compute usage.
- Regression: A statistically significant drop in a guardrail metric compared to a baseline.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Model onboarding owner: model-owner@redwood (ML team).
- Eval harness owner: applied-ml-platform@redwood (Applied ML).
- Quantization profiles owner: inference-compiler@redwood (Runtime team).
- Regression triage lead: slo-ops@redwood (SRE).
- SLA for triage initial response: 4 business hours for severity P1 regressions, 24 hours for P2.

Pre-onboarding checklist (before adding a model to the eval harness):
1. Confirm model artifact provenance and license compliance.
2. Ensure model metadata includes architecture, tokenizer, expected sequence length, and supported ops.
3. Provide a minimum reproducible inference example (README + script).
4. Supply initial performance profile (latency percentiles, memory footprint) on supported hardware.
5. Assign an on-call owner and a code owner for onboarding PRs.

Onboarding procedure (step-by-step):
1. Create an onboarding ticket in the applied-ml backlog and assign the model-owner and eval-harness owner.
2. Add the model to the eval harness manifest (manifest format described in "Eval Harness Standards").
3. Provide an initial prompt set (see Prompt Set Guidelines below) and baseline metrics run.
4. Run standard eval suite: correctness (task-specific metrics), contextual safety (toxicity, privacy), and performance (latency/p99, throughput, mem).
5. Review results with applied-ml and runtime teams; record baseline in model registry and link to PR.
6. If baseline passes guardrails, proceed to quantization profiling. If not, iterate with model owner on fixes.

Prompt set & benchmark design guidelines:
- Prompt taxonomy: each prompt set must be labeled with capability tags (e.g., summarization, instruction-following, code-generation, arithmetic, world-knowledge, safety-edge-cases).
- Minimum sizes: small exploratory set (50 examples), core validation set (500 examples), and an expanded stress set (2k+ examples) for regression monitoring.
- Diversity requirements: cover languages (for multilingual models), token-length buckets (short/medium/long), and common real-world formats (JSON, code, markdown).
- Templates and dynamic prompt generation: include templated variants for slot-filling and adversarial perturbations to test robustness.
- Labeling: provide ground-truth where possible; otherwise use consensus human evals or a separated reference model + human-in-the-loop scoring.

Example prompt set metadata (plain text table):
| field | example | notes |
|--|--|--|
| name | summarization-news-core | short identifier |
| tags | summarization, long-form, en | capability tags |
| size | 500 | core validation minimum |
| owner | research-nlp@redwood | contact |
| baseline_model | redwood-7b-vanilla | model used for baseline |

Benchmark metrics (recommended):
- Correctness: BLEU/ROUGE for seq2seq tasks, exact-match/F1 for QA, pass@k for code where applicable.
- Semantic similarity: SBERT cosine or embedding-based similarity with a calibrated threshold.
- Safety: toxicity (Perspective API), hallucination rate (entity contradiction checks), PII leakage counts.
- Robustness: performance under token drop/typo/noise perturbations.
- Operational: median latency, p95/p99 latency, GPU memory, tokens/sec, and cost-per-token.

Quantization profiles and validation:
- Objective: reduce memory and cost while maintaining acceptable quality loss (configurable per-customer SLO).
- Profile naming: <base-model>-q{bits}-{strategy}-{calibration>-e.g., redwood-7b-q4f16-kmeans-calib
- Supported strategies: symmetric per-tensor, per-channel, kmeans-aware, mixed-precision (e.g., 8-bit key/value, 4-bit activations).
- Validation steps for each profile:
  1. Run the full core validation prompt set and compare primary metrics to baseline.
  2. Run safety and adversarial stress sets.
  3. Record latency, mem, and token throughput on target hardware.
  4. Compute delta thresholds (see Guardrails below).
- Auto-reject criteria: any profile that increases PII leakage or toxicity by > 2x baseline, or drops core correctness metrics beyond configured thresholds.

Quality guardrails (thresholds and actions):
- Guardrail categories and default thresholds (configurable per-model):
  - Correctness drop: no core metric drop > 3% absolute (or 5% relative if baseline < 10%).
  - Safety regressions: toxicity/PII/counts: zero tolerance for increases > 1% absolute when baseline low; configurable for tolerant models.
  - Latency: p95 latency must not exceed baseline p95 by >20% for latency-sensitive configs.
  - Memory oversubscription: any profile that causes OOM on supported hardware is rejected.
- Actions on guardrail breach:
  1. Automated notification to model-owner and applied-ml channel with attached diffs and example failures.
  2. If P1 (safety or severe correctness): immediate rollback to last-known-good profile and temporary production fallback to cheaper/higher-accuracy model.
  3. Start regression triage (see below) if P2/P3 with 24-72h target resolution windows.

Regression triage playbook (templates and runbooks):
- Trigger events: scheduled nightly/regression-monitoring job or manual alert from QA/customer.
- Triage severity matrix:
  - P1: Safety (toxic output, PII leak) or catastrophic correctness (regression > 10%) in production traffic.
  - P2: Core metric regression between 3-10% or latency regressions causing SLO violations.
  - P3: Minor degradations or single-route anomalies.
- Initial response (first 4 hours for P1):
  1. Acknowledge in incident channel and assign triage lead (SRE or model-owner).
  2. Collect failing examples, baseline comparisons, and deterministic reproduction steps from eval harness.
  3. Attach logs: inference traces, token-level logprobs, top-k alternatives, and any model-diff artifacts.
  4. If clearly caused by quantization change or model deploy, revert to previous stable profile immediately.
- Investigation checklist (48-72 hours):
  - Re-run failing prompts under baseline and candidate profiles to rule out non-determinism.
  - Check tokenizer and pre/post-processing changes. Tokenization drift is a common vector.
  - Validate model weights: checksum and model artifact provenance.
  - Compare activation distributions for suspect layers if instrumentation available.
  - Test under synthetic traffic matching production payload distributions (lengths, concurrency, headers).
- Resolution and follow-up:
  - Document root cause and remediation steps in the regression ticket.
  - If code or model changes are required, produce a patch and a canary rollout plan.
  - Update prompt sets if the failure is due to uncovered edge cases; schedule new regression benchmarks.
  - Postmortem for P1s: complete within 7 days with action items and owners.

Automation and tooling recommendations:
- Integrate eval harness runs into CI: every model PR must run core validation (fast smoke) and schedule nightly full-suite runs.
- Automated diff reports: generate a human-readable artifact with summary metrics, failing examples (red/green), and suggested rollback actions.
- Canary rollouts: support A/B route based on routing policy (latency/cost/region) and automatic abort on guardrail breaches.
- Observability: include token-level cost/latency breakdowns in dashboards and link eval results to model registry entries.

Example commands and snippets:
- Run a core validation locally (example):
  ./eval_harness/run_eval.sh --model redwood-7b --promptset summarization-news-core --profile q4f16 --out results.json

- Quick JSON summary of fails (pseudo):
  cat results.json | jq '[.examples[] | select(.passed==false) | {id: .id, prompt: .prompt, baseline: .baseline_output, candidate: .candidate_output}]'

- Manifest example (one-line YAML in manifest):
  - id: redwood-7b
    repo: s3://models/redwood-7b
    tokenizer: tiktoken-v1
    baseline_profile: fp16

Acceptance criteria before production promotion:
- Core validation: all core metrics within configured deltas.
- Safety checks: no increase in toxicity/PII counts beyond thresholds.
- Quantization: throughput/memory improvements meet target while maintaining acceptable quality.
- Operational: p95 latency and error rates within SLO on target infrastructure.
- Documentation: onboarding PR includes model manifest, prompt set links, baseline figures, and rollback plan.

Documentation & references:
- Link to Eval Harness Standards page and example manifests.
- Quantization Profiles Best Practices (see related pages).
- Regression triage templates (runbooks and incident channels).

FAQ (short):
Q: What if a prompt set lacks ground truth?
A: Use human-in-the-loop scoring with a cross-rater consensus and record inter-rater agreement (Cohen\u2019s kappa).

Q: How do we choose delta thresholds per model?
A: Start with the defaults in this playbook and adjust based on model criticality and customer tolerances; document the reasoning in the model registry entry.

Q: Who can approve a new quantization profile?
A: Model-owner + applied-ml owner + inference-compiler owner must sign off; for high-risk models an SRE reviewer is also required.

Maintenance and iteration cadence:
- Review prompt sets quarterly and refresh stress/adversarial examples every major release or after a production incident.
- Re-run quantization validation whenever model weights are updated or tokenizer changes.
- Conduct a regression game-day every quarter to exercise the triage playbook and update SLAs.

Appendix (checklist summary):
- Onboarding checklist: license, metadata, README, performance profile, assigned owner.
- Core evals to run: correctness, safety, latency, memory, adversarial.
- Guardrails to enforce: correctness delta, safety/PII increases, latency bounds.

If you have questions or need access to the eval harness trial cluster, contact applied-ml-platform@redwood.
